objects_changed.name: acme_notify_sms
objects_changed.change: Removed Twilio credentials embedded in the api.request URL; URL now built from $env.TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and auth header from $env.TWILIO_BASIC_AUTH. Env var names are my choice.

templates_considered: SEC-012 no_secrets_in_code: fits the ask directly (hardcoded keys and credentialed URLs), used as-is

rules.covers: No API keys, tokens or credentialed URLs written as literals in any object definition or agent settings; the Twilio case from the ask

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Bare 32-hex Twilio auth token in a header or param with no recognisable shape
Generic hardcoded passwords (e.g. password = "...") not in a known credential shape
Values inside environment variables are not scanned by default
Rotating the exposed Twilio credential and setting env vars

assumptions: Env var names TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and TWILIO_BASIC_AUTH are new; the customer must set them
The customer wants the function fixed in this change, since the approved plan said build all of it
Advisory enforcement is the right default for a new policy per the skill
confusions: The catalogue says aws and twilio match identifiers rather than secrets, but gives no pattern for a bare Twilio auth token; unclear whether any pattern catches it
The skill's rule for writing a $env reference in place of a literal does not show the exact XanoScript for concatenating an env value into a URL; I copied the style from acme_get_tracking headers
wished_for: A pattern or literal check for generic password and bare hex token shapes
An example of a $env reference used inside a url string
why_confidence: The literal credential check covers the Twilio incident and the general API key case, but a bare hex auth token or a generic password can pass unflagged. The dry run was clean, but no policy evaluation has been run, so findings are unverified.
